blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic HR has moved well beyond the old rhetoric of "people are our most important asset." Every HR director now has to demonstrate, with evidence, how the people agenda moves commercial, operational and financial outcomes. That demands a rare combination of skills: genuine fluency in the language of the business, the analytical discipline to isolate the impact of people interventions, and the credibility to challenge senior leaders when short-term pressures risk undermining long-term capability.

Rarely has the HR function been under more scrutiny — and rarely has it mattered more. Warm words about culture no longer buy a seat at the table; a defensible link between the talent agenda and the numbers does.

The best HR leaders do three things relentlessly. They connect the talent agenda to concrete business outcomes. They make bold, sometimes unpopular choices about where to invest and where to withdraw. And they build coalitions with finance, strategy and operations, because no people initiative succeeds in isolation from the rest of the business.

items.q: According to the text, what must every HR director now demonstrate?
options: That people are the most important asset
That the culture programme is popular with staff
How the people agenda moves commercial, operational and financial outcomes
That HR spending has been reduced year on year
items.why: "demonstrate, with evidence, how the people agenda moves commercial, operational and financial outcomes."

items.q: Which three things do the best HR leaders do relentlessly?
options: Connect the talent agenda to outcomes, make bold investment choices, and build coalitions
Cut costs, defend headcount and report to the board
items.why: O texto lista exatamente esses três: conectar a resultados, fazer escolhas ousadas e construir coalizões.

items.q: The phrase "no longer buy a seat at the table" suggests that HR credibility now depends on…
options: evidence and a defensible link to the numbers
the size of the HR team
items.why: Inferência: o texto contrapõe "warm words" a "a defensible link… to the numbers" — é a evidência que compra o assento.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Calling people 'our most important asset' is enough to prove HR's value.
HR should be able to isolate the impact of its interventions.
HR sometimes has to make unpopular investment choices.
People initiatives depend on other functions to succeed.
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata essa retórica como ultrapassada — "moved well beyond the old rhetoric."

items.q: What does "where to withdraw" imply about strategic HR choices?
options: That HR must sometimes stop funding certain areas, not only add to them
That HR should avoid all difficult decisions
That HR should withdraw from board meetings
That investment decisions are made only by finance
items.why: Inferência: escolher onde investir E onde recuar significa cortar deliberadamente, não só somar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando a estratégia de pessoas ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. I know the question on everyone's mind, and I'll put it plainly: does this leadership investment pay for itself? So let me not hide behind culture language. Let me show you the numbers.

Over the last three years, the business units that ran the accelerated leadership programme grew their operating margin roughly four points faster than the units that didn't. Now, I'm not going to claim the programme alone did that — there are other variables. But when we control for market and for size, a clear gap remains, and it is not a rounding error.

David, I know finance has been sceptical, and honestly, you should be — the burden of proof sits with me, not with you. What I'm asking for today is not a blank cheque. It's a two-year commitment, with agreed metrics we review every quarter, and the right to pull the funding if the impact isn't there.

Because the real risk isn't spending on capability. The real risk is arriving at the growth targets in 2028 without the leaders in place to deliver them.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Sophie choose to answer the question about whether the investment pays for itself?
options: By showing the numbers rather than hiding behind culture language
By deferring the decision to finance
By appealing to the importance of culture
items.why: "let me not hide behind culture language. Let me show you the numbers."

items.q: What does Sophie concede about the margin difference she presents?
options: That the gap disappears once you control for size
That the programme alone explains all of it
That the programme alone did not cause it — other variables exist
items.why: "I'm not going to claim the programme alone did that — there are other variables." Ela isola o impacto com honestidade.

items.q: What exactly is Sophie asking the board for?
options: A two-year commitment with quarterly metrics and the right to pull funding
Approval to hire more HR staff
A blank cheque for leadership development
items.why: "a two-year commitment, with agreed metrics we review every quarter, and the right to pull the funding."

items.q: Why does Sophie tell David that his scepticism is fair?
options: Because the programme has already failed
Because she accepts that the burden of proof sits with her
Because finance controls all decisions anyway
items.why: Inferência: ela ganha credibilidade assumindo o ônus da prova — "the burden of proof sits with me, not with you."

items.q: According to Sophie, what is the REAL risk?
options: Reaching the 2028 targets without the leaders in place to deliver them
items.why: Inferência: ela reenquadra o risco — não é gastar, é chegar às metas sem líderes prontos.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She managed to articulate the strategy in a single, memorable sentence." To articulate means to…
items.why: Articulate = articular, exprimir com clareza e coerência.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Without analytical rigour, HR's claims sound like ___ rather than evidence."
items.why: Sem rigor analítico, a afirmação vira mera opinião — o oposto de evidência.

items.q: "The programme's effect was hard to isolate because the market moved at the same time." To isolate the impact means to…
options: separate out what one factor alone caused
hide the results from the board
items.why: Isolate the impact = isolar o impacto, separar o efeito de um fator dos demais.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Cutting graduate hiring funds this year's margin but erodes future ___ — that is the ___ the board must weigh."
items.why: Capability = capacidade/competência futura; trade-off = a escolha estratégica entre ganho agora e capacidade depois.

items.q: "No people initiative succeeds without a coalition across finance and operations." A coalition is…
options: an alliance of parties working towards a shared goal
items.why: Coalition = coalizão: aliança de partes que atuam por um objetivo comum.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando a HR defende sua estratégia no conselho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the two-year budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We agreed the metrics, and now HR has to follow through." To follow through means to…
options: carry the commitment all the way to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "The CFO pushed back on the leadership spend." He…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente vetar de vez.

items.q: "None of the soft-skills workshops will move the needle on retention." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível e mensurável.

items.q: "Before I ask for funding, let me make the case with the data." To make the case means to…
options: present a reasoned argument in favour of something
items.why: Make the case = argumentar de forma fundamentada a favor de algo.
